question.text: Securities in a client's demat account can be blocked through which methods?

answer.text: By the client directly through the depository's online system, by an e-DIS/eDIS mandate, or through the DP based on a physical or digitally signed DIS or POA/DDPI authorization
Only by the client using the depository's online system
Only through the stock broker, with no client or DP involvement

explanation.text: The Logic: Securities in a client's demat account can be blocked by the client directly through the depository's online system, by an e-DIS/eDIS mandate, or through the depository participant based on a physical or digitally signed Delivery Instruction Slip (DIS) or POA/DDPI authorization. The Trap: Each "Only..." option lists one valid blocking method, but the depository system supports several alternative methods so that the mechanism is accessible regardless of how the client interacts with the DP. Note: The keyed option was rewritten as a standalone source-grounded method list (instead of "All of the above"), and the unsupported "online is the most efficient" pro-tip was removed along with the Cross-Exam Context paragraph.
